Rule-list handler: for the turn player, then the other side, finds the first face-up spell/trap zone 5-9 holding card_id with slot flags bits 1 and 3 clear, an effect keyed card_id on the slot, and whose card is not already in the chain or trigger queue (duel_core_is_card_in_chain_or_queue); queues its trigger (duel_core_chain_queue_field_trigger(side, slot, 0, 0)) and, when that is refused, removes the marker (card_id, kind 1); returns 1. Returns 0 when none. Side effects: trigger queue or marker removal. No direct caller (rule list, presumably 0x09dedaf8; hypothesis medium).

Rule handler of card 0x1c40: for each side (turn player first) with a player-wide record keyed 0x1c40 (duel_core_get_effect_value(side, 0x0b, 0x1c40) >= 0, value = card reference), returns that card from the Graveyard to the hand when it is there (duel_core_post_announce_slot(side, 0x1c40 + is_trap), duel_core_add_graveyard_card_to_hand_no_source), removes the record and returns 1. Returns 0 when no side has the record. Side effects: announce, card to hand, record removal. No direct caller (rule list 0x09dedaf8).

Rule handler: shuffles the Deck (duel_core_post_shuffle_deck) of the first side (turn player first) whose player slot (11) carries effect key and returns 1; returns 0 when neither does. Side effects: shuffle command. Callers: 1 (duel_effects_check_rule_list).

Rule handler: for each side (turn player first) syncs the hand-reveal state: if the hand should not be revealed (duel_core_is_hand_revealed == 0) posts duel_core_post_set_hand_reveal(side, 0) and returns 1 if that changed something, otherwise shuffles the hand (duel_core_post_shuffle_hand) and returns 1 when player flag bit 2 (0x09e2a648) is set; if it should be revealed posts duel_core_post_set_hand_reveal(side, 1) and returns 1 on a change. Returns 0 when nothing changed. Side effects: reveal/shuffle commands. No direct caller (reached through a function pointer).

Rule handler: calls duel_core_check_targeting_links(side, slot) for every occupied Monster Zone 0-4 of both sides (turn player first) and returns 1 at the first non-zero result, else 0. Side effects: those of the check. No direct caller (reached through a function pointer).

Rule handler: for Monster Zones of both sides (turn player first) holding a Gemini monster (card_db_is_gemini) whose effect is not active, removes all its counters of type 0 and returns 1 when that changed something, else removes its record keyed 0x1db0 (value 1) and returns 1 when one was removed. Returns 0 when nothing changed. Side effects: counter change, record removal. No direct caller (rule list 0x09dedaf8).

Rule handler: calls duel_core_enforce_slot_controller(side, slot) for every occupied Monster Zone 0-4 of both sides (turn player first) and returns 1 at the first non-zero result (a control change was posted), else 0. Side effects: those of the enforcement. No direct caller (reached through a function pointer).

Chooses which of a card's duplicate effect records duel_effects_find_record uses, by card id and link state: 0x1eea u16 +0x0c - 1; 0x1ec4 u32 +0x14 != 0; 0x1e5a and 0x0eb2 slot == 0x0e (Graveyard); 0x1e1f 1 when the location in byte +0x15 is >= 5; 0x1da5 1 for event code 5, 2 for event 1; 0x1da4 1 for event 2, 2 for event 5; 0x1d98 event 0x17; 0x1d0a event 0x25; 0x1d9f 0 when the instance at u16 +0x14 is its own, else 1 or 2 by byte +0x16 bits 2-3; 0x1db0 and 0x1cf4 u16 +0x0c == 2; 0x1cb1 event 0x12 (1 own slot, 2 another); 0x1cb0 0 event 8, 1 event 0x16, else 2; 0x1ca3 selector 1 and u32 +0x14 != 0; 0x1534 event != 0; event-code tests for groups: == 2 (0x1f1f, 0x1cfc, 0x1cd8, 0x1b08, 0x19bd, 0x1877, 0x1370, 0x1286), == 0x12 (0x1ebe, 0x1caf), == 0x16 (0x1dc8, 0x1da2, 0x1d6d, 0x1c86, 0x1c4d, 0x1b51, 0x1ab0), == 8 (0x1e2a, 0x1dc1, 0x1d38, 0x1d08, 0x1c75, 0x1c74, 0x1c73, 0x1b8f), == 5 (0x1f1e, 0x1e75, 0x1e37, 0x1cf2, 0x1cf1, 0x19c0, 0x1911, 0x1315, 0x11cf, 0x0e8c); otherwise Spirit monsters (card_db_is_spirit) with selector 1 return 1 unless the event code is 5; all others 0. Returns the variant index. No side effects. Callers: 1 (duel_effects_find_record).

Runs the activation test of link ctx: looks up its effect record (duel_effects_find_record); without one returns true. Otherwise increments the nesting counter 0x09e28f80 and makes ctx the current link (0x09e28e44): the slot +0c condition, when present, gives r = cond(ctx, arg) (default 1); when r is 1 and a slot +08 target filter exists, r becomes whether the filter accepts some field slot 0-10 of either side whose flags bit 3 is clear. Restores 0x09e28e44 and the counter and returns r > 0. Side effects: none lasting (0x09e28f80 and 0x09e28e44 are restored), apart from those of the called handlers. Callers: 32 (duel_effects_confirm_optional_trigger, duel_effects_resolve_shared_16fe_x7, ai_handler_check_candidates_0e88_1b5c, duel_core_chain_build_step, ...); exported (2 import stubs without callers).

Hand Special Summon rule: returns 4 (action bit "Special Summon by own procedure") when the card of instance ref (id = 0x09e2bbcc + ref x 6 & 0x3fff) may be Special Summoned by side, otherwise 0. Order: 0 for an empty or non-monster card; a card named by Prohibition (duel_effects_is_card_prohibited) sets reason 0x10 in 0x09e2d288 (local side only); duel_core_can_special_summon false sets reason 0x11; then duel_core_can_summon_card_from(side, id, location of ref) and the summon locks of duel_core_call_can_summon_under_rivalry (tested on the opponent's side for 0x1d9a, 0x1cda, 0x1a92, 0x1578, which are summoned there). Monsters for which thunk_card_db_is_summoned_without_polymerization is set (extra-deck procedures) return 4 from duel_effects_check_fusion_materials(side, 4, id) for Fusions or duel_core_can_synchro_summon_card otherwise. All others go through a compare chain of about 120 ids with per-card tests: the Toons 0x154a/0x12a5/0x127d-0x127f need duel_core_has_face_up_spell_trap_12be and then the Normal Summon tribute rule by Level (<= 4 a free zone, 5-6 one, 7+ two duel_core_count_tributes_needing_zone); field-material procedures store side/controller, card id (+0x04), clear the tribute count (+0x0a) and set flag +0x34 bit 1 in the summon record 0x09e290bc and count slots with duel_core_filter_procedure_material, duel_core_filter_send_procedure_material, duel_core_filter_familiar_possessed_material, duel_core_filter_mist_valley_return_material or duel_core_filter_alien_skull_tribute; graveyard-banish procedures compare duel_effects_count_candidates(side, id, 0/1) against per-card minimums with the record byte +0x38 (0x09e290f4) as a mode flag; others count Graveyard Attributes, face-up monsters, hand size (+0x0c), field cards, LP (> 500 for 0x17c8/0x17c7) or player flag bits 21/17 of +0x120. Most branches return 0 when duel_core_count_free_monster_zones is 0. Side effects: reason code 0x09e2d288, the summon record fields above (probe values) and 0x09e290f4. Callers: 4 (duel_core_get_hand_action_mask, duel_core_list_cond_main_phase_special_summon, ai_try_hand_special_summons, duel_core_collect_list_activations); exported (2 import stubs without callers).

Preparation routine for Ancient Gear monsters (default route of duel_core_summon_prepare), on summon record sub-step +0x36. Step 0: a face-up summon whose instance is the value of marker 0x19ad on the summoner's player slot, with a free zone, needs no tributes (+0x0a = 0, returns 1); otherwise it tests duel_core_get_summon_set_mask_ex in modes 2, 3 and 0 to decide whether card 0x19b2 can stand in for a tribute: impossible -> answer 0, mandatory -> answer 1, optional -> yes/no question (message 0xfa) naming 0x19b2 (duel_core_find_card_entry_by_id). Step 1: answer 0 goes to step 4; otherwise a hint formatted from text 0x13 with the 0x19b2 name and duel_core_begin_select_tributes(side, 1, 0, duel_core_filter_gear_castle_tribute). Step 2: not confirmed returns -1 (cancel); confirmed announces and tributes the chosen slot (duel_core_tribute_own_slot). Step 3 sets the tribute count +0x0a = 0 and the summoning card +0x08 = 0x19b2 and returns 1. Step 4 does the same mode test for card 0x1e03 and step 5 applies it: with the answer a Level 7+ monster continues at tribute step 0x0a (one tribute), a lower one needs none (returns 1); without it, step 0 of duel_core_summon_select_tributes. Other steps delegate to duel_core_summon_select_tributes. Returns 1 done, 0 running, -1 cancelled. Side effects: summon record, answer 0x09e2d248, tribute, hints. Callers: 1 (duel_core_summon_prepare).

Preparation routine for monsters Special Summoned by banishing cards (0x1e6e, 0x1e31, 0x1dbd, 0x1db4, 0x1d91, 0x1d86, 0x1c81, 0x1c2b, 0x1c2a, 0x1bc9, 0x1bc8, 0x1bb5, 0x19ca, 0x18b4, 0x16c5-0x16cb, 0x16e4, 0x1483-0x1487, 0x1466). Without the procedure flag (summon record +0x34 bit 1) it is duel_core_summon_select_tributes. Otherwise, on sub-step +0x36: step 0 opens a timing batch, takes the count from duel_core_get_procedure_banish_count, formats a hint with the required Attribute or Type name (texts 0xd6-0xd9, 0x162; hint 0x56 for 0x1e31, 0x1dbd, 0x1db4, 0x1c81, 0x1bb5) and stores the count in +0x37; step 1 opens the candidate list (duel_core_open_card_list mode count + 6, at most 0x26; 0x47 for 0x18b4; 0x1e6e passes ref + pass << 16); step 2 banishes each picked candidate (duel_core_get_picked_candidate) until +0x37 exceeds the answer count 0x09e2d248: from the Graveyard with duel_core_banish_graveyard_card, from the hand with duel_core_banish_hand_card_as_cost, from the field with duel_core_request_banish_slot_no_cause; step 3 stores the answer in +0x0c for 0x18b4, runs a second pass (step 4 = step 0 with pass byte +0x38 = 1, other Attribute/Type) for 0x1e6e, 0x1c2b, 0x1c2a, 0x1bc9, 0x1bc8, 0x16e4, 0x16cb, 0x16c9, otherwise closes the timing batch, sets the tribute count +0x0a to 0 and returns 1. Returns 0 while running. Side effects: summon record bytes +0x0a/+0x0c/+0x37/+0x38, banish moves, hints, timing batch. Callers: 1 (duel_core_summon_prepare).

Material stage for extra-deck monsters with their own procedure (contact fusions, on summon record sub-step +0x36). Step 0 stores the Fusion id 0x09e29050 and instance 0x09e29054, the material count 0x09e29058 and the material codes (0x09e2906c + i x 4) from the recipe table (duel_effects_get_fusion_material_count/_code), clears the pick count 0x09e29064 and shows hint 0x4c for Neos and Gladiator Beast monsters, 0x3a for 0x1ceb, 0x46 otherwise. Step 1 opens card selection with filter 0x09da8654 (for 0x1ceb the third argument allows ending after two picks). Step 2: not confirmed -> 0x1ceb with two or more picks fixes the count and continues, else restarts at step 0; confirmed -> duel_effects_add_fusion_material(instance); more needed -> step 1; 0x1ceb keeps selecting while duel_effects_find_fusion_material(side, 4) finds another candidate (variant 0x09e29070 = 7). Step 3 builds the slot mask of the ring 0x09e28e50 picks: Neos/Gladiator Beast turns face-down materials face-up (duel_core_post_set_face) and returns them to the Deck (duel_core_request_return_mask_to_deck), 0x1ceb sends them to the Graveyard (duel_core_request_send_mask_to_graveyard_as_cost), every other monster banishes them (duel_core_request_banish_mask). Step 4 shuffles the searched Decks; step 5 adds instance marker 0x15b4 (kind 3, value material instance) per material to the Fusion and posts command 0x4e (id, instance, count | 0x100). Returns 1 from step 6 on, 0 while running. Side effects: 0x09e29050-0x09e29070, ring, requests, commands. Callers: 1 (duel_core_summon_prepare).

Synchro material selection on the summon record sub-step +0x36 (0x09e290f2). Step 0 stores the Synchro id 0x09e29050 and instance 0x09e29054, the minimum material count 0x09e29058 (duel_core_get_synchro_min_materials), clears the pick count 0x09e29064, sets the Level still to cover 0x09e28f64 to the printed Level and shows hint 0x3a with it. Step 1 opens card selection (duel_core_begin_select_cards(side, id, 0, filter 0x09cbe5bc)). Step 2: not confirmed -> UI event 0x31 and back to step 0; confirmed -> the picked slot's Level (duel_core_get_level) goes to 0x09e28f68; for card 0x1f32 whose slot flag bit 8 is clear it tests duel_core_try_synchro_material with its Level and with 2, forcing Level 2 (answer 1) or asking yes/no (message 0xfa), then step 0x0a stores the answer in slot flag bit 7 and uses Level 2 when set. Step 3 posts UI event 0x30 (side, slot, instance), appends the instance to the ring 0x09e28e50 at 0x09e28e4c + count, subtracts the Level; at <= 0 the material count becomes the number picked and step 4 follows, otherwise step 1. Step 4 builds the slot mask, announces a 0x1f32 used at Level 2, posts command 0x4c (slot, material instance, Synchro instance) per material and command 0x61 (Synchro instance | 0x8000, 0, 8), and sends the materials to the Graveyard with duel_core_request_send_mask_to_graveyard_as_cost (link with the controller bit). Step 5 posts command 0x4e (id, instance, count | 0x200). Returns 1 from step 6 on (done), 0 while running. Side effects: 0x09e29050-0x09e29064, 0x09e28f64/68, ring 0x09e28e50, slot flag bit 7, commands, send request. Callers: 2 (duel_effects_resolve_1ef0, duel_core_summon_prepare).

Preparation stage of the summon procedure: dispatches on the card id of the summon record (0x09e290bc, id +0x04) to a card-specific routine or the generic one and converts its result. Gods and other three-tribute monsters (0x1386, 4999, 5000, 0x1f39 ...) start duel_core_summon_select_tributes at sub-step 0x1e; card lists go to duel_core_summon_step_nimbusman, _send_procedure, _mist_valley_return, _evil_dragon_ananta, _banish_dark_graveyard_cost, _fog_king, _return_graveyard_monsters, _grinder_golem, _swift_gaia, _familiar_possessed, _cost_procedure, _banish_field_procedure, _neo_bubbleman, _material_procedure, _opponent_tribute, _behemoth, _banish_procedure, _three_named_tributes, _one_material_procedure, _gate_guardian and _moth_procedure. Inline cases: 0x194c tributes one monster then discards a hand card (step 0x0f, duel_core_discard_hand_card_as_cost); 0x17c8/0x17c7 by procedure (+0x34 bit 1) pay 500 LP (duel_core_pay_lp), else tributes; 0x154b/0x13b5 first ask whether to Tribute Summon (duel_core_summon_step_ask_tribute_summon_option, the answer 0x09e2d248 selects sub-step 0 or 0x1f); 0x1f0c, 0x147b and others re-check duel_core_get_summon_set_mask_ex with modes 2 and 0 and may ask a yes/no question (message 0x72) to summon without tributes (then tribute count +0x0a = 0 and +0x08 = own id). 0x1cd0/0x19aa by procedure clear the position bits. Default: Synchro -> duel_core_summon_prepare_synchro; extra-deck procedure monsters -> duel_core_summon_prepare_contact_fusion; a procedure summon -> tributes; Elemental Hero -> duel_core_summon_step_necroshade; Ancient Gear -> duel_core_summon_step_gear_castle_tribute; Dinosaur (race 9) -> duel_core_summon_step_big_evolution_pill; otherwise duel_core_summon_select_tributes. A negative routine result sets record flag +0x34 bit 3 (cancelled), posts UI event 0x2b and returns 1; result 1 re-initialises the record with duel_core_init_procedure_summon(side, ref, position, tribute count) when +0x34 bit 1 is set, else duel_core_init_normal_summon(side, ref, tribute count, position == Attack), and returns 1; otherwise returns 0 (call again). Side effects: summon record, LP, hand, UI events through the routines. Callers: 1 (duel_core_run_summon_procedure).

For a monster with a Special Summon procedure, gives the AI the material filter and count: writes *count (default 1; 2 or 3 for cards needing several, e.g. 3 for 0x1e20, 0x1a65, 0x138a, 0x111c, 0x1bb8, 0x19a5) and selects a selection callback by id (duel_core_filter_mist_valley_return_material, _hand_monster_to_send, _hand_dark_level_5_plus, _alien_skull_tribute, _procedure_tribute_material, _neo_bubbleman_material, _familiar_possessed_material, _banish_field_procedure_material, _opponent_tribute_material, _named_tribute_from_table, _procedure_material_with_zone, _gate_guardian_tribute, _moth_procedure_material, _send_procedure_material, or duel_core_filter_tribute_candidate for the Toons 0x154a/0x127f/0x12a5/0x127d); *count = 0 when the card has no rule. The filter address is left in the return register (Ghidra shows no return value; hypothesis, confidence medium). Side effects: writes *count. Callers: 1 (ai_try_hand_special_summons).

After a summon, queues the summoned card's own "when summoned" trigger: does nothing unless the card in the record's slot (summon record 0x09e290bc: controller bit 1, slot bits 2-5) is face-up (slot +0x08). Builds a 32-bit summary: bits 0-8 card instance (record bits 13-21), bit 9 controller, bits 10-13 slot, bit 14 position, bit 15 face-up, bit 16 summoner differs from controller, bit 17 proper summon (type +0x06 bit 0), bits 18-19 distinct tributes (+0x0b, max 3), bits 20-23 source location. Per event (6 Normal/Tribute Summon, 7 Flip Summon, 8 Special Summon) per-card id lists decide whether the card triggers (tribute-count conditions, Gladiator Beast summoner +0x08, proper-summon bit, summoned from the Graveyard or hand ...); event 7 gives code 2 for cards with a FLIP effect (thunk_card_db_get_flip_kind). A positive card calls duel_core_chain_queue_trigger(card id | slot << 16 | controller << 31 | event << 25 | 0x200000, instance, summary); for a FLIP card whose trigger was queued it also posts command 0x62 (card id). Cards 0x190a and 0x1488 queue their own triggers (0x190a once per set bit 7-9 of its player-slot effect value, which it removes). Card 0x1a1f only gets a kind-2 marker. No return value. Side effects: trigger queue, command 0x62 and marker posts. Callers: 3 (duel_core_summon_step_special, duel_core_summon_step_normal, duel_core_summon_step_flip).

Execution stage of summon kind 1 (Normal Summon/Set/Tribute Summon) for the summon record 0x09e290bc, a state machine on the sub-step byte +0x36 (0x09e290f2). Step 0/1: a position of 2 ("ask") is taken from the answer 0x09e2d248 (Attack also sets face-up bit 6); a face-up summon posts command 0x61 (a = ref | 0x8000, b = position, c = tribute count +0x0a) and player flag 16; clears the scratch ring 0x09e28e50 entries at index 0x09e28e4c and +1 and the distinct-tribute count +0x0b; per tribute (refs at +0x0c) posts command 0x49 (slot), builds a slot mask (bit slot + side x 16) for duel_core_tribute_monsters, and accumulates per-card tribute facts into the ring (Attribute, Lightsworn, roid, Batteryman, ATK/DEF sums; the tribute's side|slot word at record +0x20). Step 2: with no zone accepted by duel_core_filter_summon_zone the card is sent to the Graveyard from its location (banished, extra deck, Deck or hand) and 1 is returned; otherwise zone selection with filter 0x09dac660. Step 3: target slot from 0x09e2d284 into record bits 2-5, posts command 0x50 (a = card id, b = position bit << 15 | face_up << 14 | slot << 1 | controller, c = ref << 1 | uses-Normal-Summon flag +0x34 bit 2), then card-specific bookkeeping that remembers the tributes (duel_core_post_set_slot_value or duel_core_post_add_marker for 0x1c62, 0x1ed8, 0x1dbc, 0x1a30, 0x164f, 5000 ...). Step 4: face-up posts command 0x2b (card id, slot, 0) and goes to 0x0a; a Set posts command 0x44 (slot, type +0x06, tribute count) and goes to 0x15. Steps 0x0a-0x0e: duel_core_summon_raise_trigger(0x20) (negation window and event 0x20). Step 0x14: done if the slot is empty; a slot carrying effect 0x12fd loses that marker and slot flag 3 and ends; otherwise command 0x44 (count + 1 for summoning card 0x19b2). Step 0x15: after duel_effects_update_negated_slots_default, duel_core_queue_summon_event_triggers(6 face-up / 9 set). Step 0x16: cards 0x13e8/0x133d summoned face-up destroy themselves (duel_core_request_destroy_slot_by_card in a timing batch); otherwise duel_core_enforce_slot_controller, re-locates the card and calls duel_core_queue_summoned_card_triggers(6). Returns 1 when finished, 0 while running. Side effects: summon record, answer flag 0x09e2d258, ring 0x09e28e50, commands and requests above. Callers: 1 (duel_core_run_summon_procedure).

Execution stage of summon kind 2 (Flip Summon), on summon record sub-step +0x36. Step 0 posts command 0x61 (ref | 0x8000, 0, 4) and player flag 16, then either command 0x34 (slot, 1, 2) when the monster is face-down in Attack Position (record byte +0x39 = 0) or command 0x33 (slot, 1, 1) when it is in Defense Position (+0x39 = 1). Step 1 posts command 0x2b (card id, slot, 1) and goes to 0x0a. Steps 0x0a-0x0e: duel_core_summon_raise_trigger(0x21). Step 0x14: done if the slot is empty, otherwise command 0x44 (slot, type +0x06, tribute count +0x0a). Step 0x15: after duel_effects_update_negated_slots_default, slot flag 21 (duel_core_post_set_slot_flag) and duel_core_queue_summon_event_triggers(7). Step 0x16: a Level <= 2 monster while 0x1255 is active is destroyed (duel_core_post_announce_card, duel_core_request_destroy_slot_by_card in a timing batch, by the opponent when the opponent controls 0x1255) and 1 is returned; otherwise duel_core_enforce_slot_controller and duel_core_queue_summoned_card_triggers(7). Returns 1 when finished, 0 while running. Side effects: commands 0x61/0x34/0x33/0x2b/0x44, player and slot flags, trigger queue, destruction request. Callers: 1 (duel_core_run_summon_procedure).

Execution stage of summon kind 4 (Special Summon by effect), also entered from kind 5, a state machine on the summon record sub-step +0x36 (0x09e290f2). Step 0: for position "ask" (record bits 7-8 = 2) either forces Attack (0x09e2d248 = 0) when duel_core_is_monster_set_allowed is false, or allocates a card instance when the record has none (index side + 2 x player word +0x04, writes the id into 0x09e2bbcc) and opens the position dialog duel_core_ask_summon_position(side, 0xf7, ref, face_up). Step 1: applies the answer; face-up posts command 0x61 (a = ref | 0x8000, or the card id for a token; b position; c = 5 + summon type +0x06 bit 0, i.e. 6 for a procedure); sets player flag 16; card 0x14d5 summoned from the Graveyard first asks for one tribute (duel_core_request_select_tributes(side, 0xffff, 1, 1); step 0x32 tributes the chosen mask 0x09e2d2fc with duel_core_tribute_monsters). Step 2: instance allocation as above; with no summon zone the card is sent to the Graveyard from its location (returns 1), else zone selection with filter 0x09dac660. Step 3: slot from 0x09e2d284; a token posts command 0x47 (a = position << 15 | face_up << 14 | slot << 1 | controller, b = card id, c = a value from the chain context 0x09e28e44 for 0xf52/0xf49/0xf47); any other card posts command 0x2c (same a plus bit 6 = proper summon, b = ref, c = a per-card value: Gladiator Beast summoner flag, material count 0x09e29058, material ATK sum 0x09e29060, source location), may add a player marker (0x1d9a, 0x1cda, 0x1578) and for activation kind 1 marks copies of 0x1666; next step 0x14. Step 0x14: done if the slot is empty; clears slot flag 3, adds per-summoning-card (+0x08) markers or slot values (about 60 ids, e.g. 0x1e15, 0x1a31 half original ATK, 0x18fe), marker 0x1d2a for a Chain Material Fusion (variant 0x09e2905c = 8), then command 0x44 (slot, type, tribute count). Step 0x15: duel_effects_update_negated_slots_default then duel_core_queue_summon_event_triggers(8). Step 0x16: duel_core_enforce_slot_controller and duel_core_queue_summoned_card_triggers(8). Returns 1 when finished, 0 while running. Side effects: summon record, instance table, answer flag 0x09e2d258, commands above. Callers: 2 (duel_core_summon_step_procedure, duel_core_run_summon_procedure).

Execution stage of summon kind 5 (Special Summon by the card's own procedure, including Synchro and contact fusion) for the summon record 0x09e290bc, a state machine on sub-step +0x36 (0x09e290f2). Step 0 opens the position dialog (duel_core_ask_summon_position(side, 0xf7, ref, face_up)) when the position is "ask". Step 1 applies the answer 0x09e2d248 (Attack sets face-up bit 6); a face-up summon posts command 0x61 (a = ref | 0x8000, b = position, c = 6); sets player flag 16; with tributes (+0x0a) posts command 0x49 (slot) per tribute, counts distinct tributes into +0x0b, stores each tribute's side|slot word at +0x20 and tributes the slot mask (bit slot + side x 16) with duel_core_tribute_monsters. Step 2: with no zone accepted by duel_core_filter_summon_zone the card is sent to the Graveyard from its location (banished, extra deck, Deck or hand) and 1 is returned; otherwise zone selection (filter 0x09dac660). Step 3: slot from 0x09e2d284, clears 0x09e2d258, computes the value c (0x1e20: +0x0c x 300, 0x1d62: x 600, 0x18b4: x 700, capped at 0xffff; 0x1ceb: material count 0x09e29058), adds a player marker for 0x1d9a, 0x1cda, 0x1a92, 0x1578, and posts command 0x2c (a = position << 15 | face_up << 14 | 0x40 | slot << 1 | controller, b = ref, c); next step 0x0a. Steps 0x0a-0x0e: duel_core_summon_raise_trigger(0x22). Later steps delegate to duel_core_summon_step_special (steps 0x14-0x16); when that finishes and the card came from the Deck (0x0d) and is 0x196b-0x196e, 0x128c or 0x112e, the Deck is shuffled (duel_core_post_shuffle_deck). Returns 1 when finished, 0 while running. Side effects: summon record, answer flag, commands 0x61/0x49/0x2c, tributes, markers. Callers: 1 (duel_core_run_summon_procedure).

Preparation routine of card 0x1cda, which is Special Summoned to the opponent's side and gives its summoner two 0xf60 tokens; runs on summon record sub-step +0x36 with the token counter +0x37. Step 0 saves the card's instance in +0x0c, makes the summoner the controller (bit 1 = bit 0), clears the source location bits 9-12, resets +0x37 and opens a timing batch (duel_core_timing_batch_begin). Step 1 allocates a token instance (side + 2 x player word +0x04, id 0xf60 in 0x09e2bbcc) into the record; with no zone accepted by duel_core_filter_summon_zone it sends the record's card to the Graveyard from its location and returns 1, otherwise opens zone selection (filter 0x09dac660). Step 2 takes the slot from 0x09e2d284, clears 0x09e2d258 and posts command 0x47 (a = face_up << 14 | slot << 1 | controller, b = 0xf60, c = 0) and command 0x44 (slot, type 5, 0). Step 3 calls duel_core_queue_summon_event_triggers(8). Step 4 repeats from step 1 for the second token, then closes the timing batch and restores the record (instance from +0x0c, controller = the opponent, source location 0x0b hand). Returns 1 from step 5 on (preparation done), 0 while running. Side effects: summon record, instance table, answer flag, commands 0x47/0x44, timing batch, trigger queue. Callers: 1 (duel_core_summon_prepare).

column2: void duel_core_apply_attack_declaration(int attacker_side, int attacker_slot, int target_side, int target_slot)
column3: Records an attack declaration in the battle state: 0x09e28620/0x09e2863c attacker side/slot, 0x09e28624/0x09e28640 target side/slot, 0x09e28628 = direct attack (target_slot >= 5), 0x09e2864c attacker instance, clears 0x09e2862c, 0x09e28644, 0x09e28648 and the two 0x48-byte battle records at 0x09e28650 (fills side, slot, instance +0x0c and the instance's 2-bit counter +0x10 for attacker and target). For a monster target it stores the target position in 0x09e28644, detaches 0x1846 records from the attacker's player slot, and for a face-down Defense Position target attaches 0x1846 (kind 4) to the attacker's player slot when link 0x1846 exists or the attacker is 0x1f25, 0x178d or (attacking the opponent) 0x152d, and record 0x1433 to the target when an active 0x1433 attacks a monster with FLIP kind 1; a face-up target with Attribute 1 gets record 0x1e92 (kind 4). Then clears the word +0x0c of the attacker side's other monster zones holding 0x1a79, sets player flag 18, duel flag 1 (duel_core_set_duel_flag) and slot flags 25 and 30 of the attacker. No return value. Side effects: battle globals, effect records, player/slot/duel flags. Callers: 2 (duel_core_cmd_declare_direct_attack, duel_core_cmd_declare_attack).

Handler of engine command 0x19 (jump table 0x09e00944) that closes an attack for slot a of side (op bit 15): b = 0 only clears slot flag bit 22; otherwise duel_core_record_attack_done(side, slot) and, when c != 0: for an active attacker among 0x1e92, 0x1e50, 0x1c1f, 0x1ab3, 0x1a79, 0x1a4e, 0x1958, 0x1644, 0x1505 whose slot flag bit 2 is clear it attaches record 0x1505 (kind 1, value 1 after a monster attack, 0 after a direct attack, 2 for 0x1e92 against a target holding 0x1e92) when absent, and a kind-8 record keyed to the attacker on the target when the target slot still holds the attacked instance (battle record 0x09e2865c); when the attacker's player slot has 0x15ff it attaches 0x15ff to the opponent's player slot (value = not direct) and to the still-present target; then duel_core_clear_battle_scoped_effects. Clears the busy word 0x09e29904. No return value. Side effects: slot flag 22, attack records, effect records. Callers: 1 (duel_core_execute_command).

Handler of engine command 0x3e (card moved between card lists): a = instance << 6 | location << 1 | side (source list, the index found with duel_core_find_card_location); b = index << 6 | destination << 1 | destination side; c flags: bit 0 by the opponent, bits 4-5 new hand-entry bits 0-1 (hand source only), bits 6-7 passed as the banished-list insert argument. Sub-step 0x09e29908: step 0 brings a Graveyard or banished card that is not on top to the top (duel_core_graveyard_move_ref_to_top / duel_core_banished_move_ref_to_top, UI event 0x18). Step 1 (after 0x18) aborts and clears the busy word 0x09e29904 if the card is no longer at the source; otherwise sets entry +2 bit 3 from c bit 0 and clears bits 2/4/5; destinations hand/extra/Deck clear entry bit 15, bits 0-1 and 6; Graveyard destination from a non-banished list counts 0x1361 and flags 0x1574 for a monster; leaving the Graveyard (not to banishment) or the banished zone increments the instance's 2-bit counter (0x09e2bbcc + instance x 6 + 2); 0x1c4c loses entry bit 15. The hand destination appends (index = hand size), the Deck sets player flag 3; statistics 0x2c/0x2d (not when c bits 6-7 are both set), 0x2e (from the hand), 0x2f (from the Deck) when the local side moved an opponent's card. Then duel_core_zone_remove + duel_core_zone_insert, duel_core_detach_effects_of_moved_card and UI event 0x1a (instance, source, destination). Step 2 waits until no UI event is busy and clears 0x09e29904. No return value. Side effects: lists, instance table, player flag 3, effect records, statistics, UI events. Callers: 1 (duel_core_execute_command).

Handler of engine command 0x3f (field or list card sent, not destroyed, to the hand, extra deck, Deck, Graveyard or banished zone): a (0x09e290fa) = index << 6 | location << 1 | side (a field location + index < 0x0b is taken as that slot with index 0); b (0x09e290fc) = index << 6 | destination << 1 | destination side; c (0x09e290fe) flags: bit 0 by the opponent, bit 3 skip the destruction bookkeeping, bits 4-5 new entry bits 0-1, bits 6-7 remember the field slot (bit 7 stores the zone as 0xf). Step 0 (sub-step 0x09e29908) does the whole move: sets entry +2 bit 3 from c bit 0, clears bits 2/4/5, writes bits 0-1; for a non-token sent to the Graveyard it does the destruction bookkeeping of command 0x31 (player flag bit 24 for the owner's own monster, 0x165a for Level 8+, 0x14bf/0x1361 counts, 0x1574, 0x1c4c, 0x1f19) unless c bit 3; banishment clears +2 bit 6, hand/extra/Deck clear entry bit 15, bits 0-1 and 6. Copies the entry to 0x09e29910 and adds statistics 0x2c/0x2d/0x31/0x32/0x30 when the local side sent an opponent's card. The insertion position is the hand size for the hand (player flag 2 is set), otherwise a non-zero b index becomes the destination list size (append, i.e. Deck bottom) and 0 the front (Deck top); the Deck also sets player flag 3; banishment inserts at 0 or, with c bits 6-7, with (side | position << 2 | face << 1 | zone << 4) << 8 | 0x40. Then duel_core_zone_remove + duel_core_zone_insert, duel_core_detach_effects_of_moved_card and UI event 0x1a (instance, source, destination). Step 1 calls duel_core_normalize_effect_records and clears the busy word 0x09e29904. No return value. Side effects: lists, slots, player flags 2/3/24, effect records, statistics, UI event. Callers: 1 (duel_core_execute_command).

Handler of engine command 0x40 (list card placed directly in a field slot): a = instance << 6 | location << 1 | side (source, index from duel_core_find_card_location); b = offset << 6 | slot << 1 | side (target slot = slot + offset); c low byte face-up, high byte position. Sub-step 0x09e29908: step 0 brings a Graveyard or banished source card to the top of its list (UI event 0x18). Step 1 (after 0x18): clears entry +2 bits 2-6, copies it to 0x09e29910, duel_core_zone_remove + duel_core_zone_insert(side, slot, face | position << 8), duel_core_detach_effects_of_moved_card, clears slot flag bit 21 (the card may change position), posts UI event 0x1a (instance, source, destination); a Crystal Beast placed in a spell/trap zone sets bit 7 of slots holding 0x1cdf; statistic 0x1f when the local side sets a card face-down in a spell/trap zone. Step 2: for a banished source walks the player slot 11 record list (head 0x09e2a642 + side x 0xb3c) and, for kind 0-5 records whose value equals the instance, restores slot flag bit 6 (0x147f) or bit 5 (0x14f5) or re-attaches the listed marker keys (0x1eaf, 0x1bed, 0x1ad8, 0x1ad7, 0x18af, 0x185e, 0x1822, 0x1a21, 0x1a20, 0x1a1f, 0x1814, 0x17d5, 0x17d2) to the new slot; then duel_core_normalize_effect_records and clears the busy word 0x09e29904. No return value. Side effects: lists, slot, effect records, statistics, UI events. Callers: 1 (duel_core_execute_command).

Handler of engine command 0x3c (field card moved to an empty slot, possibly the other player's: control change or zone move): a = side | slot << 8 (source), b = side | slot << 8 (target), c = new face-up value. Step 0 (sub-step 0x09e29908) proceeds only when both slots are field slots (< 0x0b), else clears the busy word 0x09e29904. Step 1 copies the source entry to 0x09e29910, adds statistic 0x33 (local side took control of a monster) or 0x3b (local monster moved between own zones), copies the 20-byte slot to the target and zeroes the source, clears bit slot + side x 16 of 0x09e2bba8 and slot flag bit 25, writes face-up +0x08 = c; on a side change clears flag bit 21 and sets bit 10; retargets effect links (duel_core_retarget_effect_links(old side | slot << 8, new)); for a spell/trap target detaches the slot's effects except the kept ones (duel_core_detach_slot_effects_except_kept), clears the position +0x06 and word +0x0c, sets slot flag bit 20 when face-down, and a face-up Crystal Beast sets bit 7 of slots holding 0x1cdf; posts UI event 0x1a (instance, source, target). Step 2 normalizes effect records and clears 0x09e29904. No return value. Side effects: slots, 0x09e2bba8, effect links, statistics, UI event. Callers: 1 (duel_core_execute_command).

Handler of engine command 0x3d (two occupied field slots exchange their cards, e.g. control swap): a = side | slot << 8, b = side | slot << 8; c is overwritten. Step 0 (sub-step 0x09e29908): if either slot is empty clears the busy word 0x09e29904; otherwise swaps the two 20-byte slots, clears flag bits 21 and 25 and sets bit 10 on both, exchanges their effect links through a temporary key (duel_core_retarget_effect_links with side + 2), saves both card ids (into c 0x09e290fe and the low 14 bits of 0x09e29910) and blanks them in the slots while the animation runs. Step 1 adds statistic 0x33 when both are monster zones and posts UI event 0x1b (0, source summary, target summary: slot << 1 | side, bit 15 position, bit 14 face). Step 2 restores the card ids and normalizes effect records; the busy word is then cleared. No return value. Side effects: both slots, effect links, statistics, UI event. Callers: 1 (duel_core_execute_command).

Handler of engine command 0x33 (battle position change): side = op bit 15, a = slot, b = flip face-up value (XORed into slot +0x08), c non-zero = manual or summon change. An empty slot clears the busy word 0x09e29904. Step 0 (sub-step 0x09e29908) posts UI event 0x4a (side, slot, new position) for c != 0 with b = 0; step 1 waits, sets slot flag 3 when both b and c are set (Flip Summon: effects off until finalised) and posts UI event 0x1c (new position << 15 | new face << 14 | side | slot << 1, c == 0 && b != 0, b && c). Step 2 (after 0x1c) toggles the position +0x06 and XORs the face +0x08 with b; turned face-down -> duel_core_clear_slot_effects_on_face_change and statistic 0x1e for the local side; turned face-up -> new placement serial (0x09e2d1d0 into +0x04) and, for a monster while 0x17b1 is on the field, a kind-7 record per face-up 0x17b1 whose flag bits 1/3 are clear; when the card is now in Defense Position, card 0x1743 detaches the link records keyed to its slot from all monster slots of both sides, and slot flag bit 25 is cleared; Main Phase 1 sets the turn player's flag bit 20; with b a face-up card gets slot flag bits 15 and 19 and every flipped card bit 10; then normalizes effect records, posts UI event 0x26 and clears 0x09e29904. No return value. Side effects: slot +0x04/+0x06/+0x08/+0x10, player flag 20, 0x09e2d1d0, effect records, statistics, UI events. Callers: 1 (duel_core_execute_command).

Handler of engine command 0x34 (turn a field card face-up or face-down): side = op bit 15, a = slot, b = target face value, c flags: bit 0 show event 0x4b and remember the card (0x09e28648) when turned face-up, bit 1 disable the card's effects (slot flag 3, e.g. during a Flip Summon), bit 2 activation reveal (slot flag 1, player flag 25 for a spell or 26 for a trap, UI event 0x47), bit 3 do not toggle (only show b). An empty slot just clears the busy word 0x09e29904. Step 0 (sub-step 0x09e29908) posts UI event 0x4b (side, slot, 0 or 1) for c bits 0/2; step 1 waits, sets slot flags 1/3 per c bits 2/1, clears flag 1 when b = 0, and posts UI event 0x1c (position << 15 | face << 14 | side | slot << 1, ...); step 2 waits for 0x1c and, unless c bit 3, toggles +0x08: turned face-down -> duel_core_clear_slot_effects_on_face_change and statistic 0x1e for a local monster; turned face-up -> new placement serial from 0x09e2d1d0 into +0x04 and, for a monster while 0x17b1 is on the field, a kind-7 record per face-up 0x17b1 whose flag bits 1/3 are clear; a face-up monster gets slot flag bits 15 and 19; every case sets flag bit 10; step 3 waits for 0x47, normalizes effect records, posts UI event 0x26 and clears 0x09e29904. No return value. Side effects: slot +0x04/+0x08/+0x10, player flags 25/26, 0x09e2d1d0, 0x09e28648, effect records, statistics, UI events. Callers: 1 (duel_core_execute_command).

Handler of engine command 0x30 (card destroyed by an effect, or a card sent from a list): side = op bit 15 (0x09e290f8); a (0x09e290fa) low byte location, high byte index (for hand 0x0b, extra deck 0x0c and Deck 0x0d the index is recomputed from the instance c with duel_core_find_in_hand / _find_extra_deck_card_by_instance / _find_in_deck); b (0x09e290fc) low byte destination, bits 8-11 flags (bit 8 by the opponent), bits 12+ "clear entry bit 15"; c (0x09e290fe) card instance. Runs on sub-step 0x09e29908: step 0/1 posts UI event 0x1f (side, location | index << 8, instance; instance 0 when the destination is the Deck or extra deck) or clears the busy word when the location is empty. Step 2 (after 0x1f): for Deck/extra-deck destinations clears entry bit 15 and +2 bits 2-6 and sets the owner's player flag 3; for a list destination writes +2 bit 3 (by opponent), sets bit 4, clears bits 2/5 (bit 6 for banishment) and, for a non-token sent to the Graveyard, does the same destruction bookkeeping as command 0x31 (player flag bit 24, 0x165a for Level 8+, 0x14bf/0x1361 counts, 0x1762, 0x1972, 0x1574, 0x1c4c, 0x1f19); banishment counts 0x16da. It attaches 0x1ef4 to the opponent's player slot when a Defense Position card is destroyed with flags in the opponent's turn, adds statistics 0x11/0x12/0x2c/0x2d/0x2f, copies the entry to 0x09e29910, then duel_core_zone_remove + duel_core_zone_insert (field destination: slot flag bit 13, statistic 0x3d, a Crystal Beast placed in a spell/trap zone sets bit 7 of slots holding 0x1cdf; list: owner's list, Deck top), duel_core_detach_effects_of_moved_card and UI event 0x1a (instance | 0x50000, source, destination). Step 3 posts UI event 0x4e when flags are set and the source is a field slot; step 4 waits, calls duel_core_normalize_effect_records and clears 0x09e29904. No return value. Side effects: lists, slots, player flags, effect records, statistics, UI events. Callers: 1 (duel_core_execute_command).

Handler of engine command 0x31 (card destroyed by battle): reads side = op bit 15 (0x09e290f8), a = slot (0x09e290fa), b = destination (0x09e290fc), c bit 0 = by the opponent (0x09e290fe), and runs on the command sub-step 0x09e29908. Step 0 posts UI event 0x20 (side, slot, instance), step 1 waits until it is no longer busy. Step 2 does the move: for a non-token monster sent to the Graveyard (0x0e) from a monster zone it sets player flag bit 24 of the owner, attaches 0x165a to player slot 11 for Level 8+, counts 0x14bf and 0x1361 active-card events and handles markers 0x1add, 0x17e4, 0x1972 (BES) and slot bit 26 / record 0x197d; it attaches player-slot effects 0x17b2 (Level <= 2 without effect), 0x19b8 (Elemental Hero), 0x1ef4 (Defense Position card destroyed by the opponent in the opponent's turn) and 0x14b5 (Deck destination). For a list destination it rewrites the entry bits (+2 bit 3 by opponent, bits 2/4 set, bit 5 clear; hand/extra/Deck clears bit 15 and bits 0-1/6; Deck sets player flag 3), copies the entry to 0x09e29910, adds statistics 0x13/0x14/0x2c/0x2d/0x30/0x32 when the local side's opponent lost the card to the local side, clears the attack record word 0x09e28684 + side x 0x48 if the slot was the attacker or target, then duel_core_zone_remove + duel_core_zone_insert (field slot: sets slot flag bit 13; list: owner's list, Deck top) and duel_core_detach_effects_of_moved_card, and posts UI event 0x1a (instance | 0x70000, source, destination). Step 3 posts UI event 0x4e; step 4 waits for it, calls duel_core_normalize_effect_records and clears the busy word 0x09e29904. No return value. Side effects: field slot, card lists, player flags, effect records, statistics, attack state, UI events. Callers: 1 (duel_core_execute_command).

Handler of engine command 0x45 (card Tributed): side = op bit 15, a = field slot, b = destination, c = card instance. Sub-step 0x09e29908: step 0 waits until UI event 0x2c is free; step 1 posts UI event 0x2c (side, slot, instance) and clears 0x09e2990c; step 2 waits for it; step 3 clears entry +2 bits 2-5 (bit 6 for banishment), sets the owner's player flag 3 for the Deck, does the destruction bookkeeping of command 0x31 for a non-token sent to the Graveyard (player flag bit 24, 0x165a, 0x14bf/0x1361, 0x1574, 0x1c4c, 0x1f19), counts 0x16da for banishment, adds statistic 0x20 for the local side, copies the entry to 0x09e29910, duel_core_zone_remove + duel_core_zone_insert into the owner's destination list (Deck top), duel_core_detach_effects_of_moved_card and UI event 0x1a (instance | 0x80000, source, destination); any later step normalizes effect records and clears the busy word 0x09e29904. No return value. Side effects: lists, slot, player flags, effect records, statistics, UI events. Callers: 1 (duel_core_execute_command).

Handler of engine command 0x32 (card banished): side = op bit 15; a low byte location (field slot < 0x0b with the index in the high byte, otherwise the index comes from duel_core_find_card_location(c)); b flags: bit 0 by the opponent, bits 4-5 counter state, bits 6-7 remember the field slot (bit 7 stores the zone as 0xf); c card instance. Sub-step 0x09e29908: step 0 brings a Graveyard card that is not on top to the top (duel_core_graveyard_move_ref_to_top, UI event 0x18); step 1 waits and posts UI event 0x21 (side, location | index << 8, instance) or clears the busy word for an empty entry; step 2 (after 0x21) sets entry +2 bit 3 = by opponent, clears bits 2, 4, 5, 6, raises the entry's 2-bit counter to at least 1 when b bits 4-5 are set, counts 0x16da for both sides, and for a field source with b bits 6-7 carries the slot's kind 0-5 records keyed 0x1eaf, 0x1bed, 0x1ade, 0x1add, 0x1ad8, 0x1ad7, 0x18af, 0x185e, 0x1822, 0x1a21, 0x1a20, 0x1a1f, 0x1814, 0x17d5 or 0x17d2 over to player slot 11 (value = instance) and attaches 0x14f5 (slot flag bit 5) or 0x147f (bit 6) there; adds statistics 0x2c/0x2d/0x2f; copies the entry to 0x09e29910, duel_core_zone_remove, duel_core_zone_insert into the owner's banished list (0x0f), the insert argument carrying (side | position << 2 | face << 1 | location << 4) << 8 | 0x40 when the field slot is remembered, duel_core_detach_effects_of_moved_card and UI event 0x1a (instance, source, destination). Step 3 posts UI event 0x4e when by the opponent from a field slot; step 4 waits, normalizes effect records and clears 0x09e29904. No return value. Side effects: lists, slots, effect records, statistics, UI events. Callers: 1 (duel_core_execute_command).

Handler of the engine command that creates a card (token) in a location or rewrites an existing card's id; it is the handler of engine command 0x43 (entry 0x43 of the jump table 0x09e00944 of duel_core_execute_command; c is not read here). Side = op bit 15 (owner); a = index << 6 | location << 1 | side with position bit 15 and face-up bit 14; b = card id (bits 0-13) | instance flags << 14. When the target is free (a field slot without a card, or a list that is empty) it builds an entry (owner bit 14, bit 15 = thunk_card_db_is_special_summon_only), allocates an instance (duel_core_alloc_card_instance(owner, id, flags)) and places it: monster zone via duel_core_place_in_monster_zone (clears flag bit 21, sets bit 6 for special-summon-only cards), spell/trap zone via duel_core_place_in_spell_trap_zone (clears bit 20), or appends to the banished list, Graveyard, Deck top or extra deck. Otherwise it overwrites the card id of the entry at that location and in the instance table 0x09e2bbcc (instance flags = b >> 14). Posts UI event 0x1d (a, card id, instance) and clears the busy word 0x09e29904. No return value. Side effects: field slot or list, instance table, UI event. Callers: 1 (duel_core_execute_command).

Handler of engine command 0x05 (jump table 0x09e00944) that shows the end of the duel: side = op bit 15, a = result code relative to side (1 and 2 are swapped when side is the local side's opponent, giving the local view), b and c = win reasons of side 0 and side 1. The shown reason is the local side's (or the opponent's when the result is 2). Step 0 (sub-step 0x09e29908): for a reason in 3-10 picks the side holding it, for reason 4 posts UI event 0x40 (side, slot, i | 0x100) for each of the five card ids of the table 0x09e00930 found in that side's spell/trap zones, and posts UI event 0x3f (side, reason, 0). Step 1 (after 0x3f) writes the win reasons to player +0x30 (0x09e2a558 = b, 0x09e2b094 = c), 0x09e02cb4 = reason, 0x09e2d1f0 = result, and posts UI event 2 (result, reason). Step 2 waits for event 2 and clears the busy word 0x09e29904. No return value. Side effects: win-reason words, 0x09e02cb4, 0x09e2d1f0, UI events. Callers: 1 (duel_core_execute_command).

Handler of engine command 0x50 (hand monster Normal Summoned or Set): a = card id, b = position << 15 | face_up << 14 | slot << 1 | side, c = instance << 1 | uses-Normal-Summon bit. Step 0 (sub-step 0x09e29908) posts UI event 0x48 (side, card id, face_up). Step 1 (after 0x48) copies the hand entry (duel_core_find_in_hand(side, c >> 1)) to 0x09e29910, duel_core_zone_remove from the hand, duel_core_zone_insert into the slot (face_up | position << 8), duel_core_detach_effects_of_moved_card, sets slot flag 3 when face-up (effects off until command 0x44) and flag 10 when the hand card was revealed, and posts UI event 0x1a (instance | 1 << 16 summon, or 4 << 16 set). Step 2 attaches Cost Down (0x15c7, kind 1, its count) to the slot when it is on the player slot, calls duel_core_use_normal_summon when c bit 0 is set, sets the turn player's flag bit 20 in Main Phase 1 and posts UI event 0x1e (side, slot, position) for a Set; step 3 waits for 0x1e and clears the busy word 0x09e29904. No return value. Side effects: hand, slot, player flags 17/20, effect records, UI events. Callers: 1 (duel_core_execute_command).

Handler of engine command 0x51 (spell/trap placed from the hand): a = card id, b = face_up << 14 | zone << 1 | side, c = card instance (hand index found with duel_core_find_in_hand). Step 0 (sub-step 0x09e29908) posts UI event 0x48 (side, card id, face_up). Step 1 (after 0x48) copies the hand entry to 0x09e29910, duel_core_zone_remove from the hand, duel_core_zone_insert into the zone (face_up), duel_core_detach_effects_of_moved_card, sets slot flag 1 when face-up, and posts UI event 0x1a (instance | 3 << 16 activated, or 4 << 16 set). Step 2: a Set card sets the turn player's flag bit 20 in Main Phase 1, for a spell attaches a kind-8 record keyed to every spell/trap zone holding an active 0x1390, posts UI event 0x1e (side, slot, 0) and statistic 0x1f for the local side; a face-up card sets player flag 25 (spell) or 26 (trap), slot flag 28, uses the Normal Summon for card 0xfee (duel_core_use_normal_summon), attaches 0x198a (kind 1, value 1) to the player slot for a trap and posts UI event 0x47 (side, instance | 0x8000, 2). Step 3 waits for events 0x1e and 0x47 and clears the busy word 0x09e29904. No return value. Side effects: hand, zone, slot and player flags, Normal Summon, effect records, statistics, UI events. Callers: 1 (duel_core_execute_command).

Handler of engine command 0x44 (summon finalised): side = op bit 15, a = slot, b = summon type flags (bit 0 proper summon, bit 1 Flip, bit 2 Special, bit 3 Gemini, bit 4 summoned to the opponent's side), c = tribute count. Sets entry bit 15 of a special-summon-only monster that was properly summoned; slot flags (+0x10): Special -> bits 6 and 18; Flip -> bit 17; otherwise Gemini -> bit 14, c != 0 -> bit 5 (Tribute Summoned), face-up -> bit 16 and player flag bit 21. A face-up or Special Summoned Cloudian adds marker 0x1c67 (kind 2, value card id, or 1 when one exists) to the player slot. When the receiving side (side, or the opponent with bit 4) is the local side it adds statistics (0x1c Special, 0x1a token, 0x18 Flip, 0x19 Gemini, 0x1b Tribute, 0x16 face-up, 0x1e face-down, 0x17 Normal) and, for a face-up or Special Summon (special-summon-only cards only when properly summoned), duel_core_mark_card_used_in_duel(instance) and duel_core_call_statistics_hook. Always clears slot flag 3, normalizes effect records, posts UI event 0x26 and clears the busy word 0x09e29904. No return value. Side effects: slot and player flags, entry bit 15, effect records, statistics, UI event. Callers: 1 (duel_core_execute_command).

Handler of engine command 0x48 (jump table 0x09e00944) that shuffles a side's monsters among their zones: side = op bit 15, c (0x09e290fe) = mask of monster zones 0-4 to shuffle; a and b are kept in 0x09e2d1cc. Step 0 (sub-step 0x09e29908): with fewer than two zones in the mask it clears the busy word 0x09e29904; otherwise permutes the listed zones with a Fisher-Yates shuffle (duel_core_random), moves the effect links to temporary keys (side + 2 | slot << 8) and back to the new slots, copies the 20-byte slots into their new positions, clears slot flag bit 10 of every shuffled slot and posts UI event 0x29 (side, mask, 0). Step 1 waits for event 0x29 and clears the busy word. No return value. Side effects: monster slots, effect links, random state, 0x09e2d1cc, UI event. Callers: 1 (duel_core_execute_command).

Handler of the engine command that puts a Special Summoned card from any location into a monster zone; its argument layout equals the command 0x2c posted by duel_core_summon_step_special, and entry 0x2c of the jump table 0x09e00944 of duel_core_execute_command leads to it, so it is that command's handler: a = position << 15 | face_up << 14 | proper-summon bit 6 | slot << 1 | side, b = card instance, c = a value stored in slot word +0x0c. Step 0 (when no UI event is busy): finds the card (duel_core_find_card_location, location kept in 0x09e2990c), clears entry +2 bits 2/4/5/6, adds statistic 0x1d for the local side from the Graveyard, from a field slot decrements the instance's 2-bit counter and remembers a 0x1c40 record, duel_core_zone_remove + duel_core_zone_insert(side, slot, face_up | position << 8), duel_core_detach_effects_of_moved_card, sets slot flag 3 (effects off until the summon finishes), re-attaches 0x1c40 (kind 3), posts UI event 0x1a (instance | 0x20000), writes c to slot +0x0c (0x09e2a568 + side x 0xb3c + slot x 0x14) and sets slot flag 10. Step 1: for a proper summon of 0x1aca, 0x1809, 0x172f, 0x1636, 0x1472 or 0xea9 attaches record 0x1472 (kind 5, value c) and sets slot flag bit 12 (counts as a spell/trap); in Main Phase 1 sets the turn player's flag bit 20; increments the counter 0x09e2d240 (player flag bit 22 once it exceeds 99); from the hand with Cost Down (0x15c7) on the player slot attaches 0x15c7 with its count; counts the summon in player +0x20 (or sets its bit 16 when 0x09e2bba0 bit 3 is set); normalizes effect records and posts UI events 0x26 and 0x39 (position << 15 | face << 14 | side | slot << 1, instance). Step 2 waits for 0x39 and clears the busy word 0x09e29904. No return value. Side effects: lists, slot, player flags 20/22, counters, effect records, UI events. Callers: 1 (duel_core_execute_command).

Life Point change shared by the LP commands: gain = 0 negates the amount a (0x09e290fa) into a loss; side = op bit 15, c (0x09e290fc) cause (0 effect damage, 1 battle damage, 2 a third kind that is recorded with 0x14c0 for the turn player; hypothesis, confidence medium), card id at 0x09e290fe. Sub-step 0x09e29908: step 0 posts UI event 0x10 (side, delta, c << 8 | 1), records the card id in 0x09e2d1f8 and, when one of the special-victory monsters (0x1f39, 0x1f38, 0x1ccf, 0x1cce, 0x1b2f, 0x1b2e, 0x1986, 0x1985, 0x1729, 0x1725, 0x16ec) deals lethal damage during an attack (0x09e28628) in the other side's turn, stores the id in the opponent's player +0x2c (win reason 8); adds damage statistics (0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 6 Toon, 4/0x0c/0x0d/0x0e maxima, 0x0f lethal, 0x40 exact lethal) when the local side damaged the opponent, 0x3f when the local side lost LP and 7 for local gains. Step 1 waits for 0x10 and posts UI event 0x4d (side, delta, c); step 2 waits for 0x4d and 11 more calls (counter 0x09e2990c); step 3 posts UI event 0x10 (side, delta, c << 8); step 4 waits, then writes LP (0x09e2a528 + side x 0xb3c): a loss clamps at 0, a gain applies only while LP are non-zero; c = 2 for the turn player attaches 0x14c0 (kind 0x21, value = amount) to the player slot; statistics 8 and 9 (maximum LP, maximum lead); UI event 9; clears the busy word 0x09e29904. No return value. Side effects: LP, player +0x2c, 0x09e2d1f8, statistics, UI events. No direct caller (reached through a function pointer).

Executes the current engine command at 0x09e290f8: sets 0x09e2d234 = 1 and switches on op & 0xfff (104 cases, 1-0x68) to the handler, for example 2 duel_core_cmd_begin_turn, 4 duel_core_next_turn, 10-15 the phase-entry stubs, 0x15-0x20 the battle commands, 0x23-0x25 LP gain/loss/set, 0x29 slot flag, 0x35 attach effect, 0x43 create token / place card, 0x56 draw cards, 0x68 tutorial UI event. An unknown code clears 0x09e29904 (command finished) without doing anything. The handlers run the command over several frames and clear 0x09e29904 themselves. No return value. Side effects: those of the handler. Callers: 1 (duel_core_process_command_queue).

Builds the two 0x48-byte battle records at 0x09e28650 + side x 0x48 (attacker side 0x09e28620 / slot 0x09e2863c, defender 0x09e28624 / slot 0x09e28640) with the final Damage-Step ATK/DEF. For each side it takes a 13-word stat block from duel_core_compute_card_stats(side, slot, block, 1, 0) or, when simulate != 0, from the AI snapshot 0x09e0308c + side x 0x154 + slot x 0x44 (the defender block is zeroed on a direct attack, 0x09e28628), writes record +0 side, +4 slot, +8 position (slot u16 +6), +0x0c/+0x10 instance and generation (0x09e2bbce[inst x 6] & 3), +0x14 name id, +0x18 card id, +0x2c Type, +0x30 Level, +0x44 = 1, and clears the other fields and the two damage records at 0x09e286e0. Per side it gathers an ATK halving counter (Mirror Wall links 0x1381, active 0x1905 cards on either side, minus one for 0x1955 when the opponent has exactly 2 monsters), a DEF halving counter (0x1905), a zero flag (0x1951 against Type 4 or attribute-mask bit 4; an opponent 0x1b40 against a Fusion), an opponent 0x1d86 that halves ATK/DEF and adds one to both counters, and a flag holding the placement serial of 0x1bb3 / 0xec2 (0xec2 only for the attacker, not direct). Unless that flag is set, the attacker's own non-negated effect adds: 0x1e35 +1000 (odd count), 0x1aaf (player record) / 0x1956 (not in Attack Position) ATK halved, 0x1643 + the target's original ATK, 0x14cc +1000 and 0x13aa +2000/+2000 (simulate only, against the declared value / Type 0xf), 0x14d7 1000 x hand Dragons (simulate); then duel_core_battle_get_damage_calc_bonus(card, 1) when simulate and 0x09e2bba0 bit 0 is clear (0x1b40 zeroes the target ATK, 0x1ab3 halves the original ATK, otherwise the amount is added), 1500 per 0x1846 link, the value sum of 0x1ef2 records (0x1853 too for the target), -300 per A-Counter against an Alien plus -300 for 0x1bd9, -500 for 0x1b5b against a Six Samurai, 500 x Level difference per 0x1c38 link, and attached records 0x152d (ATK 2400), 0x14cc, 0x13aa, 0x13a7 value 1 (+3000), 0x1119 kind 4 (ATK 0); the target gets the mirror set, where 0x1621 makes the attacker's original ATK count as 200 and 0x10c6 adds one DEF halving step. Each amount is shifted by the counters (halving rounds up, negative counters double), zeroed by the flag, multiplied by -1 under Reverse Trap (0x1257 on player 0 slot 0xb) and added to words 6/7. Non-direct attacks then apply: 0x1238 links / active 0x1ac8 add half the target's ATK, an Elemental Hero with 0x18ff or a Destiny Hero with 0x1a66 gains 1000 when weaker, 0x159e equips give +2500 to a monster with ATK <= 1000 facing ATK (or DEF) >= 2500 (extra copies, or a failed condition, have their equips destroyed when apply), then 0x1bb3 (ATK/DEF at least the opponent's ATK + 100) and 0xec2 (ATK = twice the opponent's ATK) in serial order. Finally 0x150a equips are destroyed when the ATK exceeds 1299 (apply), record +0x1c/+0x20/+0x24/+0x28 receive original and final ATK/DEF clamped at 0, and statistic 0x0b is maxed with the local side's ATK (apply, not simulate); apply > 1 also announces the 0x1238 equips. No VFPU code. No return value. Side effects: battle and damage records, destroy requests, statistics, announcements. Callers: 3 (duel_core_battle_compute_stats_live, ai_eval_attack, ai_sim_battle_resolve).

column2: bool duel_core_battle_is_destroyed(int attacker, int apply, int simulate)
column3: Decides whether the monster of a battle record (attacker != 0: the attacking side's record, else the other) that lost the battle is really destroyed; returns false when it is not destroyed by battle. When slot flag bit 8 is clear a per-card chain on record +0x18 applies: 0x1e84 vs Level > 3, 0x1c25 with a 0x1842 link, 0x1955 when the opponent has one monster, 0x1949 in Attack Position with an empty hand, 0x1439/0x1743 in Defense Position, 0x14e9 on equal ATK, 0x157e vs attribute-mask 0x7c, 0x14ac while linked, 0x1640 vs ATK < 1901, 0x1e06/0x147c vs ATK >= 1900, 0x13cb during its controller's turn, 0x12ac vs Level < 8, 0x19bf/0x1962/0x1913/0x1837 unless simulate, 24 ids that are never destroyed by battle (0x1e90, 0x1dbd, 0x1cf3, 0x1cf2, 0x1cf1, 0x1cae, 0x1c6e-0x1c71, 0x1c62, 0x1c60, 0x1b8c, 0x1a00, 0x19ff, 0x1855, 0x1770, 0x1645, 0x1598, 0x1596, 0x1441, 0x1437, 0xea7, 0xe9f, 0xe8a), then effective id 0x1d9d. Common rules: equal ATK under 0x15ec (not spell-immune), player records 0x1316/0x1d3b, 0x1805 or a kind-1 0x19b8 marker against the other side, Gravekeeper's with 0x1594, equip links 0x150a/0x17ff/0x18df/0x1992/0x1a18/0x1c8e, a 0x1957 link, a Destiny Hero while a Special-Summoned 0x1a05 exists, slot records 0xec2/0xecd/0x1b33/0x1b2c/0x1e3b, player record 0x1e17, an Attack-Position card_db_is_clear monster with 0xec4, a Frog with 0x1db1, a Level <= 3 Type-2 monster with 0x1dbb. Substitutes then keep it on the field: 0x1b6b with a non-zero slot value, 0x1f31/0x1e9e/0x1e1c/0x18f1/0x1ca4 once and 0x1f36 twice per 0xfb6 count (markers 0xfb6 kind 2 and its id kind 4 when apply; skipped when simulate), counter type 0x13 with 0xeb8 active (marker 0xeb8), or an equipped substitute (a kind-12 monster equip on 0x1ad6-0x1ad8/0x1aae-0x1ab1/0x1284/0x1281, or an active Union/0x1e02/0x1d23/0x1d16/0x1b58/0x1989 equip, marked 0x15b3 kind 4 when apply); such a substitution sets record +0x3c = 1. Side effects: record +0x3c, and markers/announcements only when apply. Callers: 1 (duel_core_battle_resolve).

Returns true when a battle damage record (damage: +4 source side, +8 source slot, +0x0c damaged player, +0x10 damaged slot) is prevented, examined for the attacker's battle record (attacker != 0) or the defender's (false at once for the defender on a direct attack). When the monster's slot flag bit 8 is clear: 0x1e6e/0x1e50 prevent damage to the other player; 0x13cb damage to its own slot during its turn; 0x1f31, 0x1bb5, 0x18b8, 0x1642, 0x14af, 0x1cf3, 0x1cf2, 0x1cf1, 0x1441 damage to its controller; 0x1c61 all; 0x1bb6 when attacking; 0x1cb7 (card or slot record) damage to the other player. For the attacker's record: damaged player's records 0xead/0x1d3b/0x18aa/0x1cdc; against the other side records 0x1316/0x1805, a 0x1890 record on the source slot or a kind-1 0x19b8 marker; field spell 0x10f4 with 0x13f7 on the damaged side when the attacker deals it; 0x17fe while the damaged player has monsters; field 0x1a0c while the damaged player's block +0x108 > 3. Damage to the monster's own controller: Type 0x11 with an active 0x175e, a Destiny Hero name while a Special-Summoned 0x1a05 exists, a substituted monster (+0x3c) with a 0x1989 link. Finally a monster without effect of Level <= 3 under the damaged player's 0x179d, or a kind-4 0x151e marker on the attacking player (Last Turn battle). No side effects. Callers: 1 (duel_core_battle_resolve).

Parses one line of a .ydq duel setup by its first character and fixed byte offsets (strncmp + sscanf %d). `[END]` returns 1; every other line returns 0. LimitTurn sets 0x09e2d1e4 (0xffff for n <= 0, else turn + n - 1); TurnPlayer sets 0x09e029a8; Turn sets the turn counter 0x09e2d1e0 = digit - 1; PlayerLP

writes the LP word of player block p & 1; Phase calls duel_core_set_phase from the first letter (D 0, S 1, M 2, B 3, E 5). CardInHand/Deck/Fusion/Grave/Exclude

entries (a line with `=` right after the player digit is ignored) build a 4-byte list entry (card id low 14 bits, bit 14 side, serial from block +0x04 in bits 7-14 of the high half, incrementing +0x04), initialise the 6-byte instance entry in 0x09e2bbcc and append to the deck (+0x10; hand entries also increment +0x0c), extra deck (+0x18), Graveyard (+0x14) or banished (+0x1c) list; for players 2/3 the hand/deck/extra ids go to the partner table 0x09e02cb8 + (p & 1) x 300 and set 0x09e2d1fc. CardInGame

_SSS writes the slot card id and the _Face (+8), _Turn (+6), _Owner (byte +1 bit 6), _Param (+0x0c) and _Flag (+0x10 bits 0x1/0x40/0x80/0x800/0x1000) fields. EquipActNNN_* keys fill effect record NNN + 1 of the pool 0x09e2c7cc (source player/location/card id at +0, destination at +4, kind nibble at +2 from ONLYINTURN 1 to CAPTURED 12) and raise the record count 0x09e29920 to at least NNN + 1. Side effects: player blocks, instance table, effect pool, turn/phase globals. Callers: 1 (duel_core_load_ydq).

Loads a .ydq duel setup: sets both LPs to 8000 and the serial counters (block +0x04) to 1, posts command 1, then copies the text line by line (up to 255 bytes, through the newline) into a 256-byte buffer and calls duel_core_parse_ydq_line until it returns 1 (`[END]`) or the text ends. Afterwards: block +0x08 = last serial; with tag partners (0x09e2d1fc) it sets 0x09e029a0/0x09e029a4 = 1 and registers the partner table 0x09e02cb8 entries as card instances (serials after the main duellist's, table +8 = first serial). For each side and each of the 11 slots holding a card it clears the slot id and posts command 0x43 (side bit from the owner flag; a = side | slot << 1 | face-up (+8) << 14 | position (+6) << 15; b = card id), command 0x39 (slot, low, high half) for a non-zero +0x0c parameter and command 0x29 (slot, bit, 1) for every set bit of the +0x10 flags. Then command 0x35 for each equip record of the pool (destination side/location, kind << 8, source) clearing its kind, resets the record count 0x09e29920, sets the turn side 0x09e2d1d8/0x09e2d1dc from 0x09e029a8, posts command 0x56 (0xffff, hand count) for the turn player and then the other and clears both hand counters. In mode 2 (0x09e2d1f4) it also posts command 10 + phase, sets the phase to 7 and posts 0x67 (0, 5, 0) when the turn equals the last turn 0x09e2d1e4. Finally UI events 0x0f (LP) and 0x16 (0x0c-0x0f) for both sides. No return value. Side effects: player blocks, instance table, commands, UI events, turn globals. Callers: 2 (duel_core_start_mode3, duel_core_start_mode2).

Link-duel receiver: returns 1 at once while 0x09e28960 (link stopped) is set, otherwise receives one packet into 0x09e28760 (u16 type, u16 arguments from +2). No packet: returns 1 while the network is active and not aborted, else sets the error flag 0x09e2d204 and returns 0. Types 2, 3, 5, 6, 0x0a-0x0f and 0x13-0x20 decrement the outstanding-packet counter 0x09e28998. Dispatch: 1 peer error (0x09e2d204, return 0); 2 stop request (0x09e28960 = 1, replies type 3, dialog 0x0c); 3 stop acknowledged; 4 copies the turn side to 0x09e2d1dc; 5 duel_core_net_store_peer_command; 6 sets 0x09e2896c; 7 duel_core_raise_timing_event(a, b | c << 16); 8 timing batch end/begin/begin_ex for a = 0/1/2; 9 and 0x0a copy a timing queue (count 0x09e28f98, codes 0x09e28fa0, arguments 0x09e28fc0), 0x0a also resetting the window state (0x09e28e38, 0x09e29040, 0x09e2904c) and setting 0x09e28970 = 1; 0x0b/0x0e set 0x09e28974; 0x0c/0x0f submit the remote player's action (duel_core_submit_player_action(a, b, c, 3), 0x09e2d274 = remote side, 0x09e2904c = 1); 0x0d sets the window link index and 0x09e28970 = 2; 0x10 copies a 24-byte chain link to 0x09e28cb4 + a x 0x18; 0x11 sets 0x09e28e38; 0x12 duel_core_chain_add_link; 0x13/0x14 copy 0x3c bytes of action state to 0x09e290bc (0x13 also calls duel_core_summon_reset_substeps); 0x15 sets bits 2-5 of 0x09e290bc; 0x16 copies link a, raises timing 0 and records statistics for a newly activated link, then flags it for resolution (0x09e28994) or replies type 0x17 when it has no resolve handler; 0x17 copies one or two links at the chain top; 0x18-0x1b copy a link and set the flags 0x09e28984/0x09e28988/0x09e2898c/0x09e28990; 0x1c opens a prompt for the local side (0x09e2d2c0 = 1); 0x1d stores the prompt answer at 0x09e2d2d8; 0x1e requests a pending action (0x09e2d2dc = 1); 0x1f copies 16 bytes to 0x09e2d2fa; 0x20 posts command 0x22 (0x0d) for the remote side. Unknown types send packet type 1 and fail. Returns 1 to continue, 0 on a link error. Side effects: link and chain globals, timing queue, commands, packets sent. Callers: 1 (duel_core_run_duel_flow); exported (2 import stubs without callers).

column2: uint duel_core_get_monster_action_mask(int card_id, int side, int slot)
column3: Returns the cursor-menu action mask of a monster zone (0 for slot >= 5). On the opponent's side of the local player (0x09e02994 & 1 ^ 1): a face-up monster that card_db_is_usable_by_opponent accepts gets 8 when duel_effects_can_activate_face_up_card accepts a dummy context (card, side, slot, instance). On the own side: in the Battle Phase 1 when it still has attacks and duel_core_can_declare_attack holds (0x09e2d288 = 7; 8 when no attacks are left); in a Main Phase 0x10 for a Gemini summon (Normal Summon available), and with duel_core_can_change_position: face-down 0x200 (Attack Position) and 0x20 (Flip Summon possible), face-up 0x200 in Attack Position or 0x100 in Defense Position; a face-up monster with a table-3 record gets 8 when its effect can be activated (0x09e2d288 = 4). Side effects: 0x09e2d288 (action context code). Callers: 1 (duel_core_get_card_action_mask).

Selection filter wrapper for card 0x13eb: first calls the saved filter at 0x09e2d290 (with the incoming arguments; Ghidra shows no arguments, hypothesis, confidence medium) and returns 0 when it rejects. When `side` is the selecting player 0x09e2d274, it returns 0 if any monster of the other side carries marker 0x13eb with value `side` and is accepted by the saved filter (arg, other side, slot); otherwise 1. No side effects. No direct caller (reached through a function pointer, the selection filter).

column2: void duel_core_collect_list_activations(int side, int unused_arg, uint location_mode)
column3: Appends the activatable cards of one location of `side` to the candidate list (entries u32 at 0x09e29928, u16 side x 0x80 + location at 0x09e2a128, count 0x09e29920 capped at 0x1ff). location_mode low 16 bits = location, high 16 bits = mode: mode 2, or any queued timing code > 5, restricts the scan to cards whose card_db_classify_for_viewer is > 1; mode 1 also requires duel_core_timing_event_allows_card_response. It walks the 23 16-byte entries of 0x09e00dbc (card id, location, condition, activation function): player-effect entries (activation duel_core_list_activate_player_effect) are tested once with instance 0 and stored as a synthetic entry (table card id, side in bit 6, location 0x10); other entries test every card of that id in the location (from the top) when the side is the turn player in a Main Phase or the card class is > 1, and store the card's entry. In the own Main Phase without restriction it also adds, for location 0x0c, Extra Deck monsters summoned without Polymerization whose duel_core_get_special_summon_mask is non-zero, and, for location 0x0e, Graveyard cards referenced by a counter-0 kind-1 player record 0x1a04 that duel_effects_can_activate_packed_link accepts. No return value. Side effects: the candidate list and its count. No direct caller (reached through a function pointer).

Returns 1 when `side` may leave the Battle Phase (or skip it), 0 when one of its monsters is forced to attack. Outside the Battle Phase it returns 1 unless the phase is < 4 and duel_core_can_conduct_battle holds; a player record 0x16a1 or a current-turn 0x1502 always returns 1. Forced attacks (return 0): own record 0x15ff with the opponent's 0x15ff value 1 or -1 and a monster with a valid target; records 0x1669/0x14a6 or an active 0x1443 and any monster that can declare an attack; record 0x1b0a with a face-up 0x1a4b on the other side and a Level <= 4 monster not immune to Traps; an active 0xec7 affecting a monster whose Attribute (mask & 0xfe) a face-up opposing monster shares; an own 0x16bf or a monster holding record 0x1eee; 0x1a79 with a non-zero slot value and a valid target; in the Battle Phase an opposing 0x1bad (with own Attack-Position monsters) or 0x1cd4, and anywhere an opposing 0xe9f, for a non-immune monster that can declare; a monster with a 0x1d32 link. No side effects. Callers: 9 (ai_main_phase_step, duel_core_battle_step_select_attack, ai_choose_cost_by_card, duel_core_step_main_phase, ...).

Compares the attack snapshot 0x09e28730 (attacker instance and generation, the defender's 5 monster instances and generations; 0x30 bytes) with the current field. Attacker unchanged and still flagged as attacking (slot flag bit 25): the situation changed when the memcmp differs, the attacker can no longer attack, or (unless player record 0x1c4f) the target is no longer valid / a direct attack is no longer possible, or the defender has player record 0x177a or the attacker 0x1a73. On a change: if the attacker can still declare an attack it is a replay (0x09e28628 = 0, index 2, 0x09e28638 = 1, UI event 0x0c, slot flag bit 21 set, player marker 0x1c4f removed), otherwise command 0x19 (slot, 1, 1) and index 1. Attacker no longer attacking: command 0x19 and index 1. Attacker instance changed: command 0x19 for its new monster zone when it is still on the field with the same generation, then index 1.
